factual_and_methodological.summary: Mubadala primary sources confirm AED1.414tn / US$385bn AUM in 2025, AED143bn deployment, AED138bn proceeds and the 42/20/17/16/5 asset-class mix. The report separates Abu Dhabi public ownership, delegated corporate investment governance and the stronger contractual rights that can accompany private assets and infrastructure.

editorial_publication_readiness.opening: Direct mechanism-led opening; no generic sophistication claims or product-process narration.
editorial_publication_readiness.headings: Headings advance the actor-specific mechanism, constraints, contrary evidence and revision conditions.
editorial_publication_readiness.language_localization: EN and PT-BR are semantically aligned; PT-BR technical prose was localized before approval.
editorial_publication_readiness.cohesion: Argument moves from rights/capability through transmission, constraints and evidence that would revise the assessment.
editorial_publication_readiness.template_meta_qa: No prompt, QA-process, schema, renderer or roadmap leakage detected.

contextual_depth.summary: The dossier distinguishes legal rights, operating capability, transmission, substitutability and institutional constraints rather than relying on scale or reputation.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: At least two analytical tables, one quantitative chart, one causal flow and one mind map in both locales.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: Visuals encode sourced quantities or mechanisms defended in prose and are not combined into a synthetic power score.

contrary_evidence: A large private-asset allocation can increase illiquidity and valuation uncertainty at the same time that it increases direct contractual rights.
State ownership does not establish that each cross-border transaction is directed for geopolitical or industrial-policy purposes.
limitations: Company-reported UAE GDP and employment contributions are not independent estimates of net additionality.
The degree of domestic capability transfer must be demonstrated asset by asset through production, skills, IP, suppliers or operating capability.
notes: Dedicated single-actor Strategic Actors dossier. Primary-source factual core, controlled taxonomy, bilingual parity and visual evidence reviewed; no public bundle for this ID at approval time.

en.title: Mubadala: sovereign investment, national capability and global portfolio discipline
en.deck: Mubadala combines a US$385 billion global portfolio with an explicit UAE capability-building platform. Its structural role is strongest where sovereign capital carries direct contractual rights and where domestic investments create durable operating capacity.
en.regime: Sovereign capital combines global risk-adjusted investment with explicit domestic capability formation through a portfolio with substantial private-asset exposure.
en.key_risk: State ownership can be overinterpreted as transaction-level political direction, while reported domestic impact can be mistaken for net additionality.

pt-BR.title: Mubadala: investimento soberano, capacidade nacional e disciplina de portfólio global
pt-BR.deck: A Mubadala combina um portfólio global de US$ 385 bilhões com uma plataforma explícita de formação de capacidades nos EAU. Seu papel é mais forte onde o capital soberano traz direitos contratuais diretos e onde investimentos domésticos geram capacidade operacional durável.
pt-BR.regime: Capital soberano combina investimento global ajustado ao risco e formação explícita de capacidade doméstica, com forte exposição a ativos privados.
pt-BR.key_risk: Propriedade estatal pode ser confundida com direção política de cada transação, enquanto impacto doméstico divulgado pode ser confundido com adicionalidade líquida.
